subject.title: fix(auth): cooldown inline api key billing failures

question: Should OpenClaw adopt provider-level persisted cooldown identity for inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials, including the `inline-api-key:<provider>` usage namespace and fail-closed behavior during auth/billing windows?
rationale: The reported bug is real, but the chosen fix changes existing inline-key behavior and creates public auth helper surface, so maintainer intent is needed after the mechanical availability gap is repaired.

options.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
options.body: Land this direction after direct availability callers pass the store so inline keys get cooldown protection while healthy stored profiles remain usable.

options.title: Keep profile-only cooldowns
options.body: Reject the new provider-level namespace and document migration from inline keys to auth profiles as the supported cooldown path.

options.title: Pause for narrower design
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers define the exact cooldown identity, persistence, recovery, and public helper contract they want.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
recommendation.body: Land this direction after direct availability callers pass the store so inline keys get cooldown protection while healthy stored profiles remain usable.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is product and compatibility policy for the model-auth/auth-profile boundary where steipete has the strongest history signal.
